actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by voice vote.
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by voice vote.

At the conclusion of debate, the chair put the question on the motion to suspend the rules. Mr. Huizenga objected to the vote on the grounds that a quorum was not present. Further proceedings on the motion were postponed. The point of no quorum was considered as withdrawn.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 1701.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H2116-2119; text: CR H2116-2117)
Mr. Huizenga moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill.

Referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, and in addition to the Committee on Armed Services, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.

dimensions.assessment: Affects federal agency personnel involved in foreign policy, defense, intelligence, and maritime administration.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary of State, in coordination with the Secretary of Defense, shall conduct a study

dimensions.assessment: Mandates comprehensive reporting, mapping, and strategic assessments regarding national security vulnerabilities and foreign control of ports.
dimensions.evidence: assessment of vulnerabilities of ports operated, controlled, or owned, directly or indirectly, by the United States

dimensions.assessment: Involves administrative and study costs for federal agencies, with an option to utilize federally funded research and development centers.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary of State and the Secretary of Defense may enter into an arrangement with a federally funded research and development center

dimensions.assessment: Imposes new statutory reporting, mapping, and strategy formulation requirements on multiple federal executive departments.
dimensions.evidence: To require the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of State to monitor efforts by the People's Republic of China to build or buy strategic foreign ports

dimensions.assessment: Primarily requires a one-time study and report due within one year, alongside ongoing mapping maintenance strategies.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State... shall submit... a report

missing_information: The exact cost of conducting the studies and producing the reports is not specified.
importance_detail.rationale: Requires the Departments of State and Defense to conduct a study, submit a report, and develop a global port mapping regarding strategic ports and foreign control by China.

card.label: S. 1071
card.summary: S. 1071, titled the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 and designated as Public Law No. 119-60, establishes the policies, authorizations, and funding levels for U.S. national defense programs, military construction, Department of Energy national security programs, intelligence activities, and maritime and Coast Guard operations. The legislation spans eight divisions covering defense acquisitions, authorizations for foreign affairs and intelligence, Coast Guard management and maritime safety reforms, security policies regarding foreign nations and illicit trafficking, and various other administrative matters.
